subjects.name: Early policing in the northern United States

summary: The second Behind the Police episode traces how northern US police grew from for-profit freelance constables into publicly funded forces that protected the wealthy, suppressed immigrants and broke strikes, alongside the Pinkertons and Pennsylvania State Police.

evidence.note: first formal department in Boston 1838, prompted by the 1837 Broad Street Riot
freelance, reward-driven constables in New York and Boston in the early 1800s
dangerous classes and Irish, Italians, Germans and Jews not yet treated as white
late-1800s unions and police used to break strikes framed as riots
Pennsylvania State Police created after the 1902 anthracite strike to suppress miners
1906 Windber strike where state troopers killed miners and a boy
state police search-bias data and ending of the research, 2002 to 2020
Allan Pinkerton biography, from Glasgow birth to founding the agency
Homestead strike of 1892: lockout, barge battle with Pinkertons, militia
modern Pinkerton under Securitas used against 2018 strikers and tech staff

notes: Part 2 of the Behind the Police mini-series; primary subject is the practice of early northern policing, so no roles. covered_span start is approximate (early-1800s freelance constables); the 1700s English constable system is background. Pinkerton was born in Glasgow but GB is left out of setting as the segment is brief. Philippine Constabulary model for the PSP is brief, so colonialism is not a theme. Child deaths (Windber boy, Jesse James's brother) are brief mentions.
